output.myth: Nethe was a shag who sat on the black rock under the Windward cliffs and would not go in. One autumn Tavo the Gale soaked her to the skin, and she spread her wings to the wind and said, "When the sun comes I will dry, and then I will fly home." The sun was slow that year. Ennu the Kite-Wright passed in his boat, laughed, and told her the sun was out over the sea. Nethe did not believe him and did not move. Mother Hesk, who keeps count, marked her on the Reel with a bone pin and said nothing at all. Nethe is still on her rock with her wings out, a little too damp, waiting. If you are waiting for a better day, hang your wet cloth on the line, say her name, and be patient. Hesk has counted that too.
output.verse:
Wings out on the rock,
Nethe waits for the dry sun,
still wet, still waiting.
